bug.name: A fixed coupon worth more than the cart charges the customer a negative amount

description: A $25 fixed coupon on a $15 cart produces a total of -10.
Checkout does not clamp it, so it asks the payment provider for -10.80.
The discount is subtracted from the subtotal with no floor at zero.
Percent coupons never hit this because they can only ever remove 100% of the cart.
Every existing cart test passes, because none of them uses a coupon bigger than the cart.

files.role: cartTotal subtracts the discount from the subtotal with no lower bound, so it returns a negative number
discountFor returns the raw coupon amount for a fixed coupon, never capped at the subtotal
charge takes the negative total, applies tax to it, and hands the negative amountToCharge to the caller
the only fixed-coupon test uses a coupon smaller than the cart, which is why the suite stays green

repro.expectation: Both tests fail today: cartTotal returns -10 where 0 is expected, and charge reports amountToCharge was -10.8.

why_bad: It moves money the wrong way: a negative charge is a refund, so a coupon can pay the customer out of the merchant's account.
It is trivially reachable — any published fixed coupon plus a small cart triggers it, no unusual state needed.
The payment provider, not the app, decides what a negative amount means, so the failure mode differs per provider and may not error at all.
Ledger rows written from amountToCharge go negative, so revenue reporting is wrong after the fact and has to be reconciled by hand.
The test suite stays green while it happens, so nothing alerts anyone.

solution.summary: Clamp the discount to the subtotal in discountFor so a fixed coupon can never remove more than the cart holds. One line, one function, no change to any caller or signature.
notes: Clamping in discountFor and not in cartTotal keeps the reported discount equal to the money actually taken off, so a receipt line cannot disagree with the total.
checkout.mjs is left alone: once the total cannot go below zero, the tax line and amountToCharge are correct as written.
Negative or malformed coupon values are a separate validation problem and are deliberately not touched here.

files_to_touch.change: add the over-cart coupon case from the reproduction test so the suite fails if this regresses

breaking.detail: No schema, no migration, no signature change. discountFor keeps its arguments and its return type. The only behavior that changes is the case that is already broken: a fixed coupon larger than the cart now stops at the cart value instead of going past it. Any caller relying on a negative total was relying on the bug.

safety.detail: One expression inside one pure function, no state, no I/O, covered by the reproduction test, and undone by a revert. Every existing test keeps passing because they all use coupons smaller than the cart.
risks: Historic orders already written with a negative amount are not corrected by this change and still need a data check.
If a caller elsewhere reads discountFor to display a coupon's face value, it now shows the clamped amount, which is the amount actually applied.
verification: node --test test/repro-negative-total.test.mjs — both tests pass after the change.
npm test — the four existing tests stay green.
Query orders for amountToCharge < 0 to size the historic damage.
